zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving case and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When outputting attribute values in the final JSON solution.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "rock" instead of the required "Rock" for a music genre.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that state "X is directly left of Y" as X's house number = Y's house number − 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "X is directly left of Y" as merely X < Y without enforcing adjacency.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: Treat clues that say "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as a strict ordering constraint X < Y.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a non‑adjacent left‑right relationship (e.g., "somewhere left of").
zebralogic.example: Allowing X to appear to the right of Y despite a "somewhere left of" clue.

zebralogic.title: AdjacencyWithoutOrientation
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that say "X and Y are next to each other" as |X − Y| = 1, with no implied left/right order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue states two entities are adjacent but does not specify which is on the left.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be left of Y when the clue only says they are next to each other.

zebralogic.title: ExactDistance
zebralogic.principle: For clues stating "There are N houses between X and Y", enforce |X − Y| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses separating two entities.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between" as a distance of 2 instead of the correct distance of 3.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attributes refer to the same entity, treat them as a combined attribute.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue equates two descriptors (e.g., "Carol is the hip‑hop lover").
zebralogic.example: Keeping "Carol" and "hip‑hop" as separate facts instead of linking Carol to the hip‑hop music genre.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute to that house immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue explicitly mentions a house number for an attribute (e.g., "Bob lives in house 3").
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the explicit placement of Bob in house 3 and leaving his house undetermined.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceSubstitutionBeforeOrderingAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Before applying ordering or adjacency constraints, replace any attribute reference with the concrete entity it denotes.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When ordering/adjacency clues involve attributes that have been linked via equivalence.
zebralogic.example: Applying "hip‑hop left of knitting" without first substituting the hip‑hop person (Carol) for the abstract "hip‑hop" attribute.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Ensure the final JSON output is syntactically valid: all arrays and objects are properly closed.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After constructing the solution, before returning the answer.
zebralogic.example: Missing a closing bracket in the JSON, causing a parse error.

zebralogic.title: ChildAttributeLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions a child's name (e.g., "the person whose child is named X"), treat X as the value of the child attribute for that person, linking the child name to the parent.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue refers to a child by name or connects a child name to another attribute of the parent.
zebralogic.example: Treating "the person whose child is Bella" as a separate entity from the mother, failing to assign Bella as the child's name for that mother.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or forgets to preserve the original case from the problem statement.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear, preserving case and punctuation.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model overlooks or misinterprets a clue during deduction, leading to a solution that violates a given rule.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Systematically process each clue, applying the appropriate skill (e.g., DirectAdjacency, ExactDistance) before finalizing the grid.

zebralogic.description: Missing required top‑level keys in output JSON
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the grid and omits the surrounding JSON structure required by the evaluator.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Always include both top‑level keys "reasoning" and "solution" as specified in the output format.

zebralogic.description: Malformed JSON due to missing closing brackets
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model truncates the output or loses track of nested structures, leaving brackets unbalanced.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After constructing the JSON, verify that all brackets and braces are balanced before returning the answer.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats child‑name clues as independent facts, failing to link the child name to the parent entity.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions a child's name, assign that name to the child's attribute of the referenced parent, creating an equivalence between the parent and the child name.
